sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Pro preview — Gemini API model documentation
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The exact model page lists customtools as a Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview version and explicitly describes its separate endpoint for prioritizing custom tools alongside bash. The shared specifications and linked card contain no total or active parameter count. This is a named variant relationship, not generic family resemblance.

sources.title: Gemini API release notes — February 19, 2026
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The February 19 entry explicitly launches gemini-3.1-pro-preview-customtools alongside Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview. It identifies the tool-prioritization purpose but gives no parameter count or structural-change claim.

sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Pro model card
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27, 2026 reread of the complete card. The model-dependencies and architecture sections explicitly state that Gemini 3.1 Pro is based on Gemini 3 Pro and refer to its card for architecture. Neither the original model information nor evaluation tables supply numerical total or active counts.

sources.title: Gemini 3 Pro model card — May 2026 update
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27, 2026 inspection of the complete May 2026 PDF. It describes sparse MoE routing and explicitly lists Gemini 3.1 Pro in its dependent-model family. The original Gemini 3 Pro is not a modification or fine-tune of a prior model. No total count, active count, expert dimensions or routing quantity establishes a numerical size for this base.

sources.title: Gemini API Additional Terms of Service
sources.evidence: Terms govern Gemini API access and prohibit extraction or replication of underlying model weights. They support the descriptive proprietary classification, not an open-weight license.

sources.title: Gemini Interactions API — model options
sources.evidence: Names the exact gemini-3.1-pro-preview-customtools model as Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview optimized for custom tool usage.

sources.title: Gemini CLI configuration — model definitions
sources.evidence: The exact customtools identifier has pro tier, gemini-3 family, thinking true and multimodalToolUse true; model-resolution rules explicitly select it for custom-tool use.

sources.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash model card — May 2026
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27, 2026 complete-card and comparison-table check. The explicitly labeled Gemini 3.1 Pro column contains benchmark scores, while safety sections describe relative performance. There is no total-parameter or activated-parameter column and no numerical customtools size.

sources.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash model card — September 2026
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27, 2026 complete-card check. The newer model names Gemini 3.7 Flash as its dependency and compares benchmark/safety performance; it supplies no retrospective total or active count for Gemini 3.1 Pro or customtools.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon model card — October 2026
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27, 2026 complete decoded-card check. Argon is explicitly a new model rather than a fine-tune of a previous one. Its safety comparison with Gemini 3.1 Pro contains no numerical total or active parameter count for that model or customtools.

sources.title: SFT Drives Gemini’s Safety Properties — June 13, 2026
sources.publisher: Josh Engels, Arthur Conmy, Bilal Chughtai and Neel Nanda — Google DeepMind Language Model Interpretability team
sources.evidence: First-party researcher update compares pretrained/SFT and production Gemini 3.1 Pro; it does not state customtools architecture changes or numerical model size. Inspected as training/interpretability evidence, not a source of transferred counts.

sources.title: Models.dev exact customtools record
sources.evidence: Original catalog lead inspected. Its display label and gemini-pro normalization are retained; factual specifications were checked against primary documentation.

sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Pro — Google Cloud model documentation
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Google Cloud explicitly describes customtools as an additional Gemini 3.1 Pro endpoint for custom-tool prioritization. It lists the standard preview on February 19 and its Cloud customtools endpoint on February 23; the earlier Gemini API release remains February 19. The shared specifications contain no model-weight count; parameter defaults describe sampling settings.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon Safety & Security Report
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27, 2026 full-text parameter and exact-model review. Numerous Gemini 3.1 Pro comparisons concern safety and capability rather than size. Parameter occurrences concern evaluation difficulty, model-weight protection or encoded knowledge. No total or active count for Gemini 3.1 Pro or customtools is disclosed.

sources.title: Google (Gemini) — GPT-5.6 Pro deep dive, Frontier Inference Margins
sources.publisher: Frontier Inference Margins, independent model-generated research artifact
sources.evidence: Fresh numerical search lead opened October 27, 2026. The page explicitly labels 3T total and 120B active for Gemini 3.1 Pro as speculative central assumptions in a serving-economics scenario, not measurements or Google specifications. It provides no customtools-specific size or valid count to inherit; the numbers are not adopted.

name.note: Human-readable label for the explicitly documented customtools identifier.

developer.note: Google publishes this Gemini endpoint and its model card.

family.note: Catalog normalization for Gemini Pro; official CLI places this exact variant in the pro tier of Gemini 3.

release_date.note: The Gemini API changelog launches the exact endpoint on February 19. Google Cloud lists February 23 for its own endpoint; the earlier API release is retained.

open_weights.note: Hosted API/product distribution under restrictive terms; no downloadable weights are offered for this variant.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the model/API terms; documentation and client-code licenses are separate.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 exact-ID, model-name, total-size and named-base searches found no supported nominal total. Customtools is explicitly a Gemini 3.1 Pro variant, and that model explicitly derives from Gemini 3 Pro; a supported nominal count could follow this lineage, but neither base supplies one. The 3T online lead is expressly a speculative economic assumption. Null reflects missing numerical evidence, not an exact-census or hosted-attestation requirement.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 active/activated-count searches and original/later comparison-table checks found no numerical active count for customtools or its named bases. Sparse routing is qualitative, with no expert dimensions or routing quantities sufficient to establish a count. The 120B online figure is explicitly speculative; no count is inferred from tool configuration, throughput, benchmark results or total-size estimates.

architecture.note: Explicit chain: customtools is a version on the shared 3.1 Pro endpoint page, which links the 3.1 Pro card; that card delegates architecture to Gemini 3 Pro, documented as sparse MoE Transformer. No customtools-specific structural alteration is asserted.

context_window.note: Shared documented input-token limit applies to both listed preview versions; output limit is separately 65,536.

modalities.note: Shared supported data types for the listed endpoint versions.

reasoning.note: Official CLI explicitly enables thinking for the exact customtools identifier.

tool_call.note: Exact variant is expressly optimized for custom tool selection and supports multimodal tool use.

description.value: Variant of Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview tuned to prefer custom tools in workflows that also use bash.

patch.notes: Customtools is the documented Gemini 3.1 Pro variant for prioritizing custom tools alongside bash. Its shared card identifies Gemini 3 Pro as the base and describes sparse MoE architecture. Total and active parameter counts are undisclosed for the variant and its named bases in the reviewed sources.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit: total and active counts remain explicitly null after fresh exact-model searches, reopened API/Cloud and original-card evidence, and later Google comparison/safety checks. Confirmed the explicit customtools-to-3.1-Pro-to-3-Pro lineage, but found no published numerical count to inherit. Traced 3T/120B claims to explicitly speculative serving-economics assumptions. Preserved every unrelated field assessment and correction.
